intro: The bank account in detail, loans, a first look at investing, and the tax return.
p.cuenta corriente.consejo: Your salary goes into it and your everyday payments come out of it.
p.saldo.consejo: It can be positive or negative. You check it at the cash machine or on your phone.
p.ingresar.consejo: You «ingresas» money «en» the account. It also means being admitted to hospital.
p.retirar.consejo: The opposite of «ingresar». The initial r sounds strong: «rre-ti-RAR».
p.transferencia.consejo: You «haces» a transferencia. The money goes from account to account, with no notes.
p.domiciliar.consejo: It comes from «domicilio». With a bill «domiciliado», the bank pays by itself each month.
p.comisión.consejo: It ends in «-sión», with an s: «ko-mi-SYON». You «cobras» a comisión.
p.números rojos.consejo: You say «estar en números rojos». It comes from the colour used to write debts.
p.conceder.consejo: You «concedes» a loan, a permit or a prize. The opposite is «denegar».
p.tipo de interés.consejo: It can be «fijo», which does not change, or «variable», which changes over time.
p.plazo.consejo: It has three meanings: each payment («a plazos»), a period and a deadline.
p.invertir.consejo: The e changes: «invierto», «inviertes». You «inviertes» «en» the stock market or a business.
p.ganancias.consejo: The opposite are the «pérdidas». It is almost always used in the plural.
p.declaración de la renta.consejo: You do it once a year. The result can be «salir a pagar» or «salir a devolver».
b1.texto:
**The account.** You open a **cuenta corriente**. They **ingresan** your salary, you **retiras** money at the cash machine and make a **transferencia** to pay someone. What is left is **el saldo**. If it is negative, you are **en números rojos**. The bank charges **comisiones**.

**Bills.** You can **domiciliar** the electricity bill: the bank pays it by itself.

**Borrowing.** You ask for a loan and the bank **concede** it or denies it. You pay it back in **plazos**, with a fixed or variable **tipo de interés**.

**Plazo** has three meanings: a payment (**a plazos**), a period (**a largo plazo**) and a deadline (**el plazo termina** tomorrow).

**Investing.** You **inviertes** to make **ganancias**, but you can also have losses.

**Taxes.** Each year you do the **declaración de la renta**. It comes out **a pagar** or **a devolver**.
b2.f0.texto: I want to open a current account for my salary.
b2.f1.texto: First I need your identity document.
b2.f2.texto: Do you charge any fee for keeping the account?
b2.f3.texto: We do not charge fees if you pay in your salary every month.
b2.f4.texto: I want to pay the electricity bill by direct debit.
b2.f5.texto: You can make a transfer from your phone.
b2.f6.texto: What happens if the balance goes below zero?
b2.f7.texto: The bank charges you interest and a fee.
b4.texto:
**Plazo** has three meanings: a payment (**pagar a plazos**), a period (**a corto plazo**, **a largo plazo**) and a deadline (**el plazo termina el treinta**).

**Percentages take an article**: **un tres por ciento**, **el veinte por ciento de los clientes**.

**Salir a pagar / a devolver** gives the result of the tax return: **me sale a pagar**, **me sale a devolver**. The **me** is the person affected.

**Ingresar** money **en** the account and **retirar** money **del** cash machine are opposite verbs.
b4.e0.texto: The deadline ends on the thirtieth of June.
b4.e1.texto: We pay for the car in instalments.
b4.e2.texto: Twenty per cent of the customers invest their savings.
b5.f0.texto: The bank office smells of new paper and reheated coffee.
b5.f1.texto: Behind a pane of glass, a clerk counts banknotes with quick fingers.
b5.f2.texto: On the screen, Olga's balance blinks in red.
b5.f3.texto: She clutches her bag against her chest and looks at the numbers with fear.
b5.f4.texto: Outside, the rain beats on the window as if it wanted to come in.
b5.f5.texto: The manager explains the loan to her in a soft, slow voice.
b5.f6.texto: Each instalment is a small stone on the road of thirty years.
b5.f7.texto: Olga signs the pages one by one and feels that the pen weighs a lot.
b5.f8.texto: On the way out, the cold air clears her head.
b5.f9.texto: For the first time in years, the world seems a possible place to her.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: you owe the bank money and the balance is below zero.
b6.o1: He ganado dinero en la bolsa
b6.o1.refuerzo: Those are profits; «números rojos» is the opposite.
b6.o2.refuerzo: It is an idiom: it is not about ink but about debts.
b6.pregunta: What does «estoy en números rojos» mean?
b7.frase: Tengo ____ el recibo de la luz.
b7.o0.refuerzo: It is an infinitive; «tengo» needs a participle.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «tener + participle» says the bill is already on direct debit.
b7.o2.refuerzo: It is a gerund; it is not used with «tengo» for this result.
b8.frase: Este año la declaración me sale a devolver
b8.traduccion: This year my tax return gives me a refund
b9.o0.refuerzo: That meaning is in «pagar a plazos», not in «a largo plazo».
b9.o1.refuerzo: That is another word: «plaza» is an open place in the city.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: «a largo plazo» means over a long period of time.
b11.frase: Voy a ____ cien euros del cajero.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: retirar is taking money out of the account.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Ingresar is the opposite: putting money into the account.
b11.o2.refuerzo: Invertir is putting money into something to earn more.
b11.pregunta: Which verb means to take money out?
b12.o0.refuerzo: Pérdidas is money you lose, not money you make.
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: ganancias is the money you make.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Comisiones are charged by the bank; they are not your profit.
b12.pregunta: You buy shares and make money. What do you have?
p.documento.consejo: «documento» is masculine: «el documento». The stress is on «MEN».
p.identidad.consejo: «identidad» is feminine: «la identidad». The stress is on the final «DAD».
p.cobran.consejo: «cobrar» means to charge. The «c» before «o» sounds like «k»: KO-bran.
p.alguna.consejo: «alguna» is the feminine of «algún». Before a noun it is shortened to «algún» only for masculine nouns.
p.cobramos.consejo: «cobrar» means to charge. Its stress falls on «BRA»: ko-BRA-mos.
p.comisiones.consejo: «comisión» is feminine: «la comisión». The plural ends in «-es»: ko-mi-SYO-nes.
p.ingresa.consejo: «ingresar» means to pay money into an account. The «g» before «r» is hard: in-GRE-sa.
p.cobra.consejo: «cobra» means charges or collects. It is the same verb as in «cobran».
p.pagamos.consejo: «pagamos» has the stress on «GA». The «g» before «a» is hard.
p.invierte.consejo: «invertir» means to invest. The «ie» is one sound: in-BYER-te.
p.recalentado.consejo: «recalentar» means to heat again. The prefix «re-» means again.
p.empleada.consejo: «empleada» is feminine: «la empleada». Its masculine form is «empleado».
p.billetes.consejo: «billete» is masculine: «el billete». The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.rápidos.consejo: «rápido» has a written accent on the first syllable: RA-pi-dos.
p.contra.consejo: «contra» means against or leaning on. It is a short preposition: KON-tra.
p.lenta.consejo: «lenta» is the feminine of «lento». It agrees with «voz».
p.despeja.consejo: «despejar» means to clear. The «j» sounds like a strong «h».
p.posible.consejo: «posible» is the same in masculine and feminine. The stress is on «SI».
p.negativo.consejo: «negativo» means below zero or unfavourable. The «v» is pronounced «b».
p.domiciliado.consejo: «domiciliar» means to pay bills by direct debit from the bank account.
p.declaración.consejo: «declaración» is feminine. It ends with «-ción», stressed on «ON».
p.periodo.consejo: «periodo» is masculine: «el periodo». Pronounce the «io» as one sound.
p.cajero.consejo: «cajero» is masculine. The «j» in «cajero» is a strong «h».
